introH2: 🏖️ What are Maenam and Choeng Mon like, and which zone should you stay in?
introHtml: If Chaweng and Lamai are the loud, never-sleeping side of Koh Samui, Maenam and Choeng Mon are the calm northern coast — the opposite mood in almost every way. Maenam is a long, quiet ribbon of white sand on the island's north shore, with shallow gently-shelving water that's easy for families, a fishing village behind it, the pier to Koh Phangan and Koh Tao nearby, and a Thursday-night walking street just up the road · Choeng Mon is the headland at the northeast tip — small, private coves, the closest zone to Samui Airport (~10 minutes), and a short hop from the Big Buddha and Fisherman's Village · These are the two shores the island's pioneering luxury resorts and pool villas chose, precisely for the calm and the private beaches that Chaweng can't offer · That range means the Maenam–Choeng Mon area has stays from ฿1,500 a night up into five figures, each a genuinely different experience — book the wrong zone and the mood of your trip shifts: you wanted to walk to the sand but ended up on a hillside that needs a shuttle, or wanted to be near restaurants but landed in a cut-off private bay · This guide gathers 7 Maenam & Choeng Mon hotels we've reviewed in depth, covering every budget (including one honest sunset-side pick at Lipa Noi, clearly labelled) — all built from reading real guest reviews, with the good and the honest caveats, prices compared across 3 booking sites, and direct links to book
mrtHtml: Koh Samui has no rail transit — you'll get around by rental car, scooter, songthaew (shared truck), Grab (limited) or hotel transfer · Samui Airport (USM) sits on the island's northeast, closest to Choeng Mon · The zones in this guide: Choeng Mon — the northeast headland, small quiet coves, ~10 minutes from the airport, near the Big Buddha and Fisherman's Village (Garrya Tongsai Bay, Meliá) · Maenam — the north shore, a long quiet white-sand beach near the pier and walking street, ~15–20 minutes from the airport (W on the headland, Santiburi, Maenam Resort) · Bang Por — the western end of Maenam, a quieter, more remote hillside, ~25 minutes from the airport (Code Samui) · And we include one honest outlier at Lipa Noi on the west coast for travellers who want the sunset side on a light budget, even though it isn't in the Maenam–Choeng Mon area (Lipa Bay Resort, ~40–45 minutes from Choeng Mon) · Chaweng and the nightlife are about 15–30 minutes' drive from this area; if you want to go out often, budget for taxis

entries.storyHtml: If you want one stay in the Maenam–Choeng Mon area that feels nothing like the Samui most people know, the answer is Garrya Tongsai Bay Samui (formerly The Tongsai Bay) — a 5-star, 83-room eco resort on Tongsai Bay off Choeng Mon, spread across 28 acres of a bay it owns entirely, where the original trees were deliberately kept when it opened in 1987, making it a nature-first resort before that idea caught on in Thailand. Its 9.4 is the highest score in this list · What real reviews return to again and again is the bath-with-a-view concept — nearly every room has a tub set on a balcony facing the bay — plus a clear-water private beach you can kayak and snorkel off, and staff who score an exceptional 9.9 on Booking, with many guests saying it feels like returning to a place where everyone remembers your name · The honest caveats from those reviews: the resort sprawls across a wide hillside, upper rooms mean walking or waiting for a buggy, the bay is cut off so any meal or trip out means calling a car, and the charm here is classic and natural rather than sharp-new design · Best for honeymooners and anyone who puts a quiet private bay and warm service first

entries.storyHtml: For the Samui resort with the sharpest look, W Koh Samui is the name most people picture first — 74 dark, modern pool villas tucked into green jungle on the headland above Maenam Beach, every single one with its own private pool. It opened in 2010 (originally W Retreat Koh Samui), scores 9.3 across 270 Booking reviews, and ranks #1 among Maenam-area hotels on Tripadvisor · Its signature image is WOOBAR, where the bar's infinity pool reaches out until the water melts into the sea horizon, complete with a DJ, cocktails and a sunset view the whole island drops by to photograph — plus the AWAY Spa, a private beach, and Whatever/Whenever service that earns a 9.7 staff score · The honest caveats from reviews: villas spread across a hillside and rely on a buggy that sometimes means a wait, the headland is cut off so going out for food or sights means calling a car every time, the north-facing beach is calm and shallow at low tide (better for lounging than deep swims), and value is the lowest-scoring category (8.5) because peak-season rates plus brand-priced food and drink add up · Best for honeymooners, keen photographers, and anyone who wants a private pool villa with a seaside bar all in one place

entries.storyHtml: If you've scrolled through a hundred Samui hotels and stopped on a pool that winds like a river through the whole resort, past teak buildings shaped like ships on a hillside, that image usually comes from one place — Meliá Koh Samui, the first Thailand resort from Spain's Meliá Hotels, opened in January 2020 on Choeng Mon Beach. It scores 9.1 across 1,411 reviews, the largest review base in this list · The heart of it is the swim-up loop pool that many ground-floor rooms step straight into from their own terrace, plus two-storey Boat Suites shaped like old Thai-Chinese junks with private rooftops over Choeng Mon Bay, and a fully kitted-out kids' side — kids pool, mini water park, Kids Club and a children's menu — with reviews noting that parents actually get to relax because the children are entertained all day · The honest caveats: it's a family resort, so weekends are lively with plenty of children around the pools, the ground-floor pool-access rooms have a walkway where people pass (less privacy), in-resort food runs pricey (value is the lowest category at 8.7), and Choeng Mon is a shallow, tide-dependent beach · Best for families with kids, design lovers, and short-trip travellers who want a strong resort near the airport
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For more quiet and a lounge perk, step up to THE LEVEL wing · Honeymooners should skip the ground-floor pool-access rooms people walk past — pick an upper floor or a Boat Suite with a private rooftop · Check the tide times before planning a swim, as Choeng Mon is shallow · And book ahead in high season, when rates climb clearly

entries.storyHtml: If Chaweng and Lamai are the buzz, Santiburi Koh Samui is the opposite pole — a pioneering luxury resort that chose Maenam, the quiet north shore where the sand stays soft. The whole property is 96 single-storey contemporary-Thai villas and suites scattered across more than 23 acres of tropical garden, among lotus ponds, coconut palms and mature old trees. It scores 9.1 across 374 reviews · What real reviews return to: a ~300-metre white-sand private beach, a free-form pool said to be among the largest on the island, the garden Lén Spa, and a breakfast buffet guests praise consistently — plus a calm privacy that feels more like a village than a hotel, with the resort's own 18-hole golf course about 5 minutes away · The honest caveats from reviews: in-resort food, drinks and spa run high, some villas show their age and the style is classic rather than newly modern, a few in-room details are thinner than expected, and it's about 30 minutes from Chaweng's nightlife · Best for honeymooners, families who want space, and anyone who values calm and service over brand-new design
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Match the villa to your budget — the Deluxe Garden Villa is spacious and quiet at the lowest rate, add a plunge pool with that version, and the Beachfront opens onto the sea · Breakfast is good value but other meals run high, so alternate with Maenam village or Fisherman's Village to control the budget · Golfers should book tee times ahead and ask about a stay-and-play package · And book low season for clearly lower rates

entries.storyHtml: On the Bang Por hillside at the western end of Maenam sits a hotel that makes one promise without exception — Code Samui Hotel, a 4-star design-suite hotel of 40 suites (plus villas) where every room is a suite facing the Gulf of Thailand, with floor-to-ceiling glass and a 180° sea view out to Koh Phangan on clear days. It scores 8.8 across 827 reviews · What nearly every review mentions is the infinity pool whose rimless edge meets the horizon — a photo and sunset spot — plus suites that are large across the board, most with a kitchen or kitchenette and a separate living area, minimalist design that has won an interior award, so many use it for longer stays, and staff reviews praise as warm and attentive · The honest caveats from reviews: the hotel is on a hillside, Bang Por beach is about a kilometre below and reached by shuttle, the paths inside are steep with lots of stairs, the Bang Por area is fairly remote from restaurants and you'll want a vehicle, and some reviews hit inconsistent water pressure or hot water · Best for couples and anyone who wants a spacious sea-view suite on a four-digit budget and weighs the view and design over walking straight to the sand
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a private pool at your room, choose the Pool & Terrace Suite · Groups or long-stayers should look at the Two Bedroom Penthouse with a kitchen and more space — good value split between you · If slopes are hard, ask for a room near the lobby/pool when booking · And rent a car or scooter, since Bang Por is far from shops

entries.storyHtml: If you're tired of busy Chaweng and want a quiet Samui on a light budget, Maenam Resort is the wooden-bungalow beachfront many people choose for one reason — you open the door and there's the sea · It's a long-standing 42-bungalow resort right on Maenam Beach, next to the luxury Santiburi, on a beach known as one of the island's quietest with the softest sand. Rates start around ฿1,600/night; it scores 8.0 from real guest reviews · What reviews mention over and over: the front-row bungalows that open onto sand and sea through a fringe of coconut palms, a calm atmosphere with no loud music and only the waves at night, friendly staff who remember guests, and a beachfront restaurant praised for both taste and price · The honest caveats to know before booking: there's no swimming pool and no TV in the rooms — it's deliberately simple — some bungalows and furniture are showing their age, the inner garden-view units feel much plainer than the front row, and the beach narrows in places and goes shallow at low tide · Best for families and travellers who want a true Maenam beachfront on a four-digit budget and don't need big-resort facilities
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Confirm a front-row beachfront bungalow when you book and at check-in — the inner garden-view units feel very different · If a pool is a must, pick one of the pooled stays in this list instead · Travelling in high season (December–February)? Book ahead and lock a free-cancellation rate, as the beachfront bungalows fill fast

entries.storyHtml: For the last pick we're adding a sunset-side option, clearly labelled — Lipa Bay Resort is not in the Maenam–Choeng Mon area, but on the other side of the island at Lipa Noi Beach on Samui's west coast, which is quiet, far from the crowds, and the side where the sun sets straight into the sea (the Maenam–Choeng Mon shore faces north and east, so it doesn't get that over-the-water sunset) · It's a small 18-room resort, bungalows and villas scattered through a beachfront tropical garden, with a pool facing the sea and a calm private beach, from about ฿1,500/night. It scores 8.0 across 105 reviews · Real reviews praise the quiet beachfront setting, the sunset from the pool every evening, garden bungalows that are good value for beachfront on Samui, and friendly staff with reasonably priced food · The honest caveats to weigh: Lipa Noi is far from Chaweng and Bophut (~40 minutes), restaurants around the resort are few and you'll need a vehicle, there's no full restaurant open at night, some rooms and decor look dated, and on some days the pool has external day-pass guests · Best for couples who'll trade the distance for a genuinely quiet, sunset-side beachfront on a light budget
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The draw is the sunset, so ask for a Sea View room or the Villa Beach Front where you can watch it in full · Rent a car or scooter, since Lipa Noi is far from shops and nightlife · Plan ahead for dinner, as there are few options around at night · And in high season book early — with only 18 rooms, the beachfront units fill fast

faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers often ask about Maenam & Choeng Mon hotels in Koh Samui

faq.q: ❓ What is the best hotel in the Maenam–Choeng Mon area?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style and budget · Going by score alone, Garrya Tongsai Bay Samui at 9.4 — an eco resort on a private bay — leads the list · For a private pool villa with a seaside bar, W Koh Samui at 9.3 · For families, Meliá Koh Samui brings a swim-up loop pool and a full kids' side, with the largest review base at 1,411 · On a beachfront budget, Maenam Resort starts around ฿1,600

faq.q: ❓ How much do Maenam & Choeng Mon hotels cost?
faq.a: The stays in this guide start at roughly ฿1,500–14,000 per night · At the light end: Lipa Bay from ฿1,500 and Maenam Resort from ฿1,600 (beachfront bungalows) · Mid-range: Code Samui ฿2,800 (sea-view suites) and Meliá ฿5,500 · At the luxury end: Garrya ฿9,500, Santiburi ฿10,000 and W Koh Samui ฿14,000 · All are approximate off-peak starting rates; peak (December–February and July–August) runs clearly higher

faq.q: ❓ How are Maenam and Choeng Mon different — and which should I pick?
faq.a: Both are on the island's north and quieter than Chaweng, but they differ slightly — Maenam is a long white-sand beach on the north shore, shallow and gently shelving for families, near the pier and the walking street (W on the headland, Santiburi, Maenam Resort) · Choeng Mon is the northeast headland with small private coves, closest to the airport (~10 min) and near the Big Buddha (Garrya, Meliá) · Pick Maenam for a long walkable beach, Choeng Mon to be near the airport and in a quiet cove · Bang Por (Code) is a more remote, quieter hillside at Maenam's western end

faq.q: ❓ Which Maenam or Choeng Mon hotel is best for families?
faq.a: The most family-built is Meliá Koh Samui ฿5,500 — a swim-up loop pool you enter from your room, kids pool, mini water park, Kids Club and a children's menu, on Choeng Mon Beach near the airport · For space and a long private beach, look at Santiburi Koh Samui, with family villas and a 23-acre garden · For a quiet budget beachfront that suits small children, Maenam Resort's wooden bungalows sit right on Maenam Beach · Note that W and Garrya lean toward couples/honeymooners more than families with young kids

faq.q: ❓ How far is the area from the airport and Chaweng — and how do I get around?
faq.a: Koh Samui has no rail transit; you'll use a rental car, scooter, songthaew, Grab (limited) or hotel transfer · Choeng Mon is closest to Samui Airport (USM) at about 10 minutes, Maenam Beach is about 15–20 minutes, and Bang Por about 25 minutes · Chaweng and the nightlife are about 15–30 minutes' drive from this area, so budget for taxis if you'll go out often · Lipa Bay at Lipa Noi on the west coast is further out, ~40–45 minutes from Choeng Mon, so a vehicle of your own helps

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book in the Maenam–Choeng Mon area?
faq.a: Koh Samui has two peaks — December–February and July–August; book 1–2 months ahead, especially for the small properties like Maenam Resort and Lipa Bay (18 rooms), where the beachfront units fill first · In low season (May–June, September–October), 1–2 weeks ahead is plenty and rates drop substantially · Every platform offers Free Cancellation rates — lock one in early if your plans might shift, then compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price
